plafonds.centre-sans: Centre of the map: no thermals at this time.
plafonds.note: The ceiling is the top of the layer where the air mixes (the boundary layer): roughly how high thermals go, often the cumulus base when clouds form. “Above ground” gives the depth of that layer; “Above sea level” adds the fine terrain, so it follows ridges and valleys. Grey means no usable thermals (layer under 300 m). NOAA GFS model for the whole Earth, on a grid of about 25 km, smoothed in between. Check on site and with the wind analysis profile, which is finer.
plafonds.absente: No forecast yet for this time.
plafonds.source: NOAA GFS model (0.25° grid), relayed by Montis

galaxie.m31.taille: About 220,000 light-years, twice the Milky Way
galaxie.m31.culture: It is rushing towards us at 110 km/s: in 4 to 5 billion years, it will merge with the Milky Way. Next to it, its two companions, M32 and M110.
galaxie.m33.culture: Third galaxy of our Local Group. Under a very dark sky, it is the most distant object you can see with the naked eye.
galaxie.lmc.type: Irregular galaxy, satellite of the Milky Way
galaxie.lmc.culture: Only visible from the Southern Hemisphere. In 1987, a star exploded there: the closest supernova seen since 1604.
galaxie.smc.type: Irregular dwarf galaxy, satellite of the Milky Way
galaxie.smc.culture: Its variable stars let Henrietta Leavitt work out, in 1912, how to measure distances across the Universe.

geologie.resume-calcaires: Cliffs, gorges and caves; little surface water
geologie.terrain-calcaires: Limestone forms cliffs, gorges and karst pavements: often good climbing rock, but karst is treacherous off the path. Water sinks in: few springs on plateaus, resurgences below. Soft marl gullies and gets slippery when wet; gypsum can collapse.
geologie.terrain-craie: Rounded hills and crumbling cliffs: keep away from the edge and the foot of chalk cliffs. Water sinks in: few streams.
geologie.resume-argiles: Soft, watertight ground, muddy when wet
geologie.terrain-argiles: Heavy soils, muddy and slippery after rain; slopes prone to landslides. Water runs off: wetlands and ponds.
geologie.resume-gres: Rough rock, in boulders and cliffs
geologie.terrain-gres: Hard, grippy sandstone: boulders and cliffs good for climbing, more fragile when wet. Dry, sandy soils.
geologie.terrain-sables: Free-draining, soft ground: sandy tracks, tiring on foot and by bike. Unstable banks.
geologie.resume-granites: Solid, grippy rock: walls, spires, boulder fields
geologie.terrain-granites: Hard, grainy rock: excellent grip, big walls and spires. Scree of large blocks. Water runs off: many lakes and streams.
geologie.resume-volcaniques: Volcanic rocks: lava flows, columns, plateaus
geologie.terrain-volcaniques: Lava flows, plateaus and columns: rock often solid, sometimes broken into prisms; angular scree. Springs at the foot of flows.
geologie.resume-gneiss: Hard, layered rock: ridges and walls
geologie.terrain-gneiss: Hard rock of old massifs: generally good rock, but layers can come away along the slope. Frequent lakes and streams.
geologie.terrain-micaschistes: Splits into plates: unstable slopes, fine scree, slippery when wet. Poor rock for climbing.
geologie.resume-schistes: Old rocks in flakes: stony paths
geologie.terrain-schistes: Split into slabs and flakes: stony paths, unstable scree, frequent rockfall. Rock often broken.
geologie.resume-ophiolites: Former ocean floor: dark green rocks
geologie.terrain-ophiolites: Green rocks (serpentinites, gabbros): rock often smooth and slippery, especially when wet. Sparse vegetation. Some contain natural asbestos: don’t break or grind the rock.
geologie.bulle-secteur: Dominant rock of the area, from the 1:1,000,000 map: the sheet’s notes give the detail.

skirando.a-propos:
The route follows OpenStreetMap ski touring routes first, then paths and tracks (BRouter, Valhalla as a fallback). It ignores snow, avalanche terrain and the bulletin: choose your line with the slope map and today’s bulletin. Time estimated for 400 m/h of ascent.
Montis helps you prepare; it doesn’t decide for you. Slope, weather and distances are estimates: check on the ground and with official sources.
Routes: OpenSkiData, © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Areas and danger levels: EAWS (CC BY 4.0).
